---
title: "Computational Mineralogy Laboratory"
---

This website contains the instructions and supporting material for the
computational laboratory activities of the **Mineral Science** course.

The laboratory environment is intentionally split into three parts:

| Resource | Purpose |
|---|---|
| **This course website** | Instructions, assignments, laboratory guides and reference material |
| **Your GitHub workspace** | Your notebooks, files, figures, results and answers |
| **CluMiner** | CRYSTAL calculations when required by a laboratory |

You do **not** need to install the scientific Python environment on your own
computer. The notebook work is carried out in a personal GitHub Codespace.

::: {.callout-important}
## New to the laboratory?

Start with **[How the laboratory works](getting-started/01-overview.qmd)** and
complete the Getting Started pages in order **before the first laboratory
session**.
:::

## Laboratory path

The practical work will progressively connect crystal structures, energetic
models, physical properties and mineral thermodynamics:

1. crystal structures, CIF files and symmetry;
2. first-principles energy and geometry optimization;
3. energy-volume data and equations of state;
4. vibrations, phonons and thermodynamic properties.

Short scientific questions are answered directly in the laboratory notebooks.
The notebooks are part of your personal workspace and should be saved and
synchronized regularly.
